interface.title: UglyMol - Agent Viewer (agent.html) with its companion Reciprocal UglyMol (reciprocal.html)
interface.stage_of_work: Model validation and inspection after refinement, plus checking diffraction indexing and lattice quality
interface.what_it_is_for: A lightweight in-browser alternative to Coot for viewing a PDB model together with its electron-density maps (its main purpose), rotating it and picking atoms, with a companion 3D viewer for reciprocal-space spot lists that shows which lattice each spot was indexed to.

data.note: agent.html auto-loads data/1YJP.pdb (GNNQQNY amyloid peptide, 1.8 Å). A toolbar button adds the built-in data/1yjp_outlier.pdb (ASN 2 OD1 moved and given B=95, GLN 5 NE2 deleted). reciprocal.html?rlp=data/rlp.csv loads 384 synthetic spots in two lattices. The real-map demo (1mru with 2mFo-DFc/mFo-DFc maps from uglymol.github.io) failed to fetch, so no electron density was ever displayed. The only uploadable test file was rlp.csv; the map input accepted it silently and drew nothing.

tree.general: Judge whether a 3D atomic model is trustworthy by looking at it directly, ideally against its experimental density, and check whether diffraction spots come from more than one lattice
tree.specific: Inspect the 1YJP crystal structure and its outlier test model in UglyMol (density maps could not be loaded in this run), and screen the rlp.csv spot list for a split lattice

features.name: Pick an atom in the 3D viewer to read its details
features.general: Double-click an item in a 3D scene to mark it, get a persistent label, and read its stored attributes in a status bar
features.specific: Double-click an atom in the UglyMol canvas: it gets a dot and an 'OD1 /2 ASN/A' label, and the top bar shows model #, atom/residue/chain, occupancy, B-factor, element and xyz position
steps: rotate/zoom until the atom is visible
double-click the atom
read occ / bf / element / pos in the top bar
repeat on more atoms; earlier labels stay on screen for comparison
serves_tasks: Spot and identify an atom with an unusually high atomic displacement (B-factor) that sits off its expected place
Find a part of the structure that is missing an expected atom

features.name: Color by a per-atom property, cycled from the keyboard
features.general: Cycle the coloring of a 3D scene through per-item properties so outliers stand out by color
features.specific: Press C to cycle coloring; the 'coloring by:' banner lists element, B-factor, pLDDT, occupancy, index and chain (only B-factor was viewed). With B-factor the B=95 atom turns dark red against blue
steps: press C
read the active mode in the 'coloring by:' banner
press again to move to the next property
double-click a highlighted atom to confirm its value
serves_tasks: Color atoms by a per-atom quality value
Spot and identify an atom with an unusually high atomic displacement (B-factor) that sits off its expected place

features.name: Overlay several models and show or hide the inactive ones
features.general: Load a second version of a structure on top of the first and switch between seeing only the current version and both together
features.specific: Model buttons add 1YJP.pdb or 1yjp_outlier.pdb as model #1/#2/…; V toggles 'Inactive models hidden' / 'All models visible', so the bonds the outlier lacks (original OD1 and GLN 5 NE2) appear as extra sticks. The hidden state did not seem to apply to a model added afterwards (063)
steps: load the reference model
click the test-case model button (added as a new model)
press V to view the new model alone
press V again to overlay both and compare
serves_tasks: Add a second model of the same structure alongside the first
Overlay two models of the same structure to see where they differ

features.name: Cycle a display option with a banner
features.general: Step one display option through its choices with a single key, while an on-screen banner names the active choice
features.specific: Examples seen: S cycles lines / trace / ribbon / ball&stick; T cycles waters as cross / dot / invisible; B cycles coot dark / solarized dark / solarized light / coot light; U toggles the unit-cell box
steps: press the option's key
read the highlighted choice in the top banner
press again until the wanted choice is active
combine with coloring (e.g. hide waters so only the outlier cross remains)
serves_tasks: Change how the model is drawn
Spot and identify an atom with an unusually high atomic displacement (B-factor) that sits off its expected place

features.name: Depth clipping slab and spin
features.general: Narrow or widen the visible depth slab of a 3D scene and toggle automatic rotation to read 3D layout
features.specific: D/F narrow and widen the clip width (shown as 'clip width: 18.7'); I toggles spinning. The help also lists </> to move the slab and K to rock (not tried)
steps: press D repeatedly to thin the slab
press F to widen it again
press I to start or stop spin
serves_tasks: Restrict depth and animate to see 3D layout

features.name: View permalink in the URL
features.general: Write the current camera into the page address so the same view can be shared and restored on reload
features.specific: Shift+P puts #xyz=…&eye=…&zoom=… into the URL; the hash is only applied when the page or model reloads, not on a hash-only change
steps: set up the view
press Shift+P
copy the URL from the location bar
open it with a full reload to restore the view
serves_tasks: Save the current view so it can be reopened

features.name: Point-cloud subset filter by lattice
features.general: Cycle a 3D point cloud between all points, the unassigned points, and each assigned group alone, to judge whether the groups are distinct
features.specific: In reciprocal.html, V cycles 'show: all / unindexed / #1 / #2'; lattice #1 (teal) and #2 (blue) are offset copies of the same grid
steps: load rlp.csv and get spots on screen (reload, wheel to zoom ~100, X)
rotate to see the doubled spots
press V to step through unindexed, #1 and #2
return to all
serves_tasks: Show each subset alone to confirm two separate lattices
Rotate the point cloud to see doubled points

features.name: Point appearance for a spot cloud
features.general: Adjust marker size and shape and toggle axes and fog to make a sparse 3D point cloud readable
features.specific: In reciprocal.html, Z/X change point size (4.0, 5.0), S switches spot shape wheel/square, A toggles axes, E toggles fog
steps: zoom until the cloud is in range (wheel to about 100)
press X until spots are visible
press S to choose spot shape
press A or E to toggle axes or fog
serves_tasks: Load the point list and make the points visible

features.name: Resolution-range filter for a spot cloud
features.general: Limit the points shown to a band of distance from the origin (a resolution range), with the limits shown on screen
features.specific: In reciprocal.html, ←/→ set the max resolution and ↑/↓ the min resolution; the banner reads e.g. 'res. limit: 13.33 - 0.04Å'
steps: press ← or → to set the high-resolution limit
press ↑ or ↓ to set the low-resolution limit
read the limits in the banner
check which spots remain
serves_tasks: Limit points to a resolution range

The reciprocal viewer opens with spots too small to see (screens/032.webp-047.jpg). t2 needs a kept frame from the rotation itself showing a readable face-on view; the drag frame 012 was not kept
